title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space and defense sectors are seeing a mix of regulatory progress and operational hurdles this week. From military GPS program shake-ups to a notable satellite launch, the landscape remains as dynamic as ever.

themes.title: Regulatory Moves Ahead
themes.body: The Office of Space Commerce is pushing forward with mission authorizations, potentially streamlining satellite operations. This could ease some bottlenecks for companies eager to deploy their technology.

themes.title: Launches and Mishaps
themes.body: Kinetica-1 successfully launched five satellites, but not without drama as the Long March 3B faced lightning strikes post-liftoff. This incident underscores the unpredictable nature of space launches, even as successes pile up.

themes.title: Military Tech Developments
themes.body: The Air Force's takeover of a troubled GPS receiver program signals a shift towards greater oversight in military tech. Meanwhile, the Space Force is refining its battle management strategies through wargames, emphasizing the importance of integration.

themes.title: Funding and Investments
themes.body: The FY27 budget markup adds $1.4 billion to space resilience, indicating a growing recognition of the need for robust space capabilities. Meanwhile, True Anomaly's $190 million Series C funding round highlights the increasing interest in commercial space ventures.
